title: Current, voltage and resistance
blurb: The big idea before the cards.

lines.caption: Electricity is electrons moving through a wire. That flow is called current, and it is measured in amperes.
lines.label: current: the flow

lines.caption: Electrons only move when something pushes them. The push is a difference in voltage.
lines.label: voltage: the push

lines.caption: Resistance holds the flow back. It opposes every kind of current.
lines.label: resistance: the opposition

lines.caption: Some current flows one way only. Alternating current keeps reversing direction.
lines.label: alternating current

lines.caption: The number of complete cycles each second is the frequency, measured in hertz.
lines.label: frequency, in hertz

lines.caption: And power is how fast electrical energy is used. It is measured in watts.
lines.label: power, in watts
